answer: Each node’s topology score weights edges by the rarity of the path’s central pearl. Standard marble routing costs one token per link traversal. An attacker dilutes this signal by flooding the network with fake nodes. The system forces them to pay a transaction fee for every redundant connection. This creates a direct financial drain on their infrastructure. Sybil clusters become economically unviable as their overhead outpaces revenue. The network treats dense, low-value clusters as a toxic oasis.
